title: How the bishop moves

D0.outcome: Says that a bishop slides any distance along a diagonal, cannot jump, and always stays on the same colour of square.

D1.outcome: When told 'bishop', marks every square a bishop can move to: it stops in front of its own pieces and may take the first enemy piece on its diagonal.

D2.outcome: In a busy position where the piece is not named, marks every square the piece on a given square can reach.

D3.outcome: Without a board, says whether a bishop can ever reach a given square (colour), and whether it gets there in one move or two.

misconceptions: A bishop can change the colour of the squares it stands on.
The bishop can jump over pieces.
A bishop can step one square straight forward like a pawn.
conditions: The bishop moves along diagonals for any number of free squares and stays on one colour of square.
It stops in front of its own piece and may take the first enemy piece on a diagonal.
contrasts: A piece on the diagonal blocks the squares behind it.
Pieces on the same rank or file as the bishop do not affect its moves.
